answer: Each identity strings one vine cord between two umber posts, locking a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files a signed log of the sag at the cord nadir, tension, and serials. An auditor recomputes sag from span and weight tables. A missing log, reused serial, or sag error over 3 percent burns the bond. A first fake costs 37 credits; the k-th costs 37+6(k-1), since each span needs its own posts, cord, and slot. The 1000th costs 6031, and 1000 fakes cost 3,034,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-cord ring fails when shared posts repeat serials. An honest keeper pays 37 once.
